$comment: Machine-readable mirror of the exhibit cards in problems/*.md. Every field here is traceable to a card in this repository or to a cited source. Nothing in this file is a claim that ProofZero verified anything it did not run. 'verified_here' is what this repo's own tools check, on a small bound. 'verified_elsewhere' is a published result this repo cites but does NOT reproduce. Keep those two fields apart: merging them would imply this repository established results it did not.

conventions.tool: Path to the tool in this repo, or null if no honest finite check exists.

verified_here.command: Exact command run in this repo's CI.
verified_here.bound: The exact finite limit that command reaches.
verified_here.runtime_sec: Measured on the maintainer's machine (Python 3.14, Windows 11). Not a promise; varies by hardware.
verified_here.checked_on: Date this repo last ran the command and observed the values below.

verified_elsewhere.bound: A published result, cited only. NOT reproduced by this repository.

conventions.open_edge: What remains unestablished. The whole point of the file.

tolerances.runtime_sec: Informational only. Never asserted by 'make verify'; timing varies by machine and must not be a pass/fail criterion.
tolerances.verification_result: Values that MUST reproduce exactly on a passing run. A change here is a real behavioural change and should fail CI.

problems.title: Riemann Hypothesis

verified_here.bound: first 20 non-trivial zeros, located by two-variable Newton iteration started off the line Re(s)=1/2

verified_elsewhere.source: Platt and Trudgian, 'The Riemann hypothesis is true up to 3*10^12', Bull. London Math. Soc. 53 (2021)

problems.open_edge: That every non-trivial zero lies on Re(s)=1/2. A verified prefix is not inductive; the property is not known to extend.
problems.note: The negative control exists to prove the checker can fail: it plants a zero at 0.8 +/- 14.13i and the tool must report deviation 0.3.

problems.title: P vs NP

verified_here.result: 323 SAT / 77 UNSAT; DPLL vs brute-force disagreements 0; invalid certificates 0

verified_elsewhere.bound: Cook-Levin: verification is polynomial, every problem in NP reduces to SAT

problems.open_edge: Whether P = NP. No super-polynomial lower bound is known for any NP problem, and no polynomial-time algorithm is known. This repo's tool is exponential-time by construction and settles nothing either way.
problems.note: The self-check is mutation-tested. Three injected faults in _dpll (false UNSAT, skipped certificate validation, inverted polarity) were each caught with a non-zero exit.

problems.title: Navier-Stokes Existence and Smoothness

verified_elsewhere.bound: weak solutions exist globally (Leray 1934; Prodi-Serrin 1957); partial regularity confines singularities to a set of small measure

problems.open_edge: Existence and smoothness of solutions in 3D for arbitrary smooth data, and the resulting uniqueness. Not computed here: no non-blow-up simulation is evidence for global regularity.
problems.note: No honest finite check exists in this repository. This is a deliberate absence, not a gap to be filled with a green cell.

problems.title: Yang-Mills Existence and Mass Gap

verified_elsewhere.bound: existence proved only in restricted settings: supersymmetric small-Higgs, and Abelian theories (not the case the Prize asks about)
verified_elsewhere.source: Witten; Jaffe and Witten; DeGrand and Jaffe

problems.open_edge: A well-defined, complete, Lorentz-invariant quantum Yang-Mills theory in 3+1 dimensions with a mass gap. A problem of existence, not approximation: computation is structurally the wrong tool.
problems.note: Empirical confirmation of the Standard Model mass gap is overwhelming but is not a proof of existence. Abelian and supersymmetric results are often overstated as progress on the hard case.

problems.title: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture

verified_elsewhere.bound: rank 0 and rank 1 established in large families, with technical hypotheses that do not generalise
verified_elsewhere.source: Kolyvagin; Skinner and Urban; Burungale, Skinner and Tian

problems.open_edge: Higher rank, unconditionally, for a single provable infinite family. Verifying individual curves to high precision bears on none of this: the conjecture quantifies over all elliptic curves over Q.
problems.note: No honest finite check exists in this repository.

problems.title: Hodge Conjecture

verified_elsewhere.bound: known in low dimension; the INTEGRAL form is false in general

problems.open_edge: The rational form in every dimension. The conjecture ranges over all smooth projective varieties of unbounded dimension and degree, so no finite sample bears on it.
problems.note: The integral and rational forms are not interchangeable. The Prize concerns the rational form.

problems.title: Poincare Conjecture

verified_elsewhere.bound: every closed simply connected 3-manifold is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere
verified_elsewhere.source: Perelman (2002-2003), via Ricci flow with surgery

problems.open_edge: None in dimension 3. Higher-dimensional analogues remain open: smooth exotic Milnor spheres exist in dimensions >= 7 (Bing 1959), the smooth 4-dimensional case is open, and Freedman's 1982 result settles dimension 4 topologically only.
problems.note: Solved. Perelman declined the prize and the Fields Medal. Included as a control: this is what a finished problem looks like, so the six open notes can be read as genuinely open by contrast.

problems.title: Collatz Conjecture

verified_here.bound: 200000 starting values, each trajectory searched with a per-start step limit
verified_here.caveat: This is a counterexample SEARCH over 200000 starting values. It is a small fraction of 2^68 and establishes nothing about the conjecture.

verified_elsewhere.bound: every n below 2^68 = 295147905179352825856 reaches 1, by verified-forcing methods over residue classes

problems.open_edge: Every n. The verified prefix is finite with no known monotonicity or induction principle that extends it. Note the scale gap: 2^68 is ~2.95e20, and this repo searches 200000 starts.
problems.note: A clean run is evidence AGAINST a counterexample up to the bound searched, and is never a proof.

problems.title: Goldbach Conjecture

verified_here.bound: every even n <= 20000, representation counts cross-checked against a naive direct count
verified_here.caveat: Twenty thousand. The published frontier is 4e18, roughly ten orders of magnitude further. This run is a regression check on the tool, not a contribution to the frontier.

verified_elsewhere.bound: every even number up to 4e18 is a sum of two primes
verified_elsewhere.source: Oliveira e Silva, Herzog and Pardi

problems.open_edge: All even integers without bound. Sieving to any finite limit says nothing about 4e18 + 2.
problems.note: The tool's own assertion caught a real truncation bug: the prime list was built only to limit//2 while pairs accumulate over the iterated prime, dropping pairs with a smaller prime above limit//2. At n=10010 the fast path reported 190 representations against the true 191. Fixed.

problems.title: Twin Prime Conjecture

verified_here.caveat: Exact counting requires no assumption. Only the INFINITY of the sequence is conjectural.

verified_elsewhere.bound: infinitely many prime gaps of bounded size; best unconditional bound is 246

problems.open_edge: Infinitude at gap exactly 2. Bounded gaps are not twins: proving infinitely many pairs at p+2k for some k <= 123 does not single out k=1. The obstruction is the sieve parity barrier, a limit of method rather than arithmetic.
problems.note: Twin counting shares goldbach_twins.py and is cross-checked the same way, for the same reason: a bounded search that silently drops cases looks exactly like evidence.

counts.with_tool_note: Five entries have a tool because goldbach_twins.py serves two entries (Goldbach, twin primes). There are six tool FILES in tools/, and four of the five tool-less entries are Millennium problems plus Poincare, which is solved and needs no tool.
counts.note: Counts exclude problems/nothing.md, which is not a problem and carries no exhibit card.
